arms: Layer selection, main (not itself a test of the hypothesis): one ridge regression per layer, layers 0 through 24 (layer 0 is the embedding output), fit on the 36 training documents pooled over all nine wrap widths, scored by held-out fit on the 12 test documents. The best layer here is the main layer, used by every ripple test and the represented-range check below; its location is recorded, never gated.

Layer selection, anchor (a separate selection from the main layer): the same ridge sweep, but fit and scored using only the width-140 documents. The best layer here is the anchor layer, used only by the anchor gate below.

Anchor gate: held-out fit quality at the anchor layer, width 140 only, on the 12 fresh test documents, checked against a band whose width is measured from 5 resplits of the 36 training documents, not guessed.
Main test, window 140 characters: the ripple statistic on the 12 test documents wrapped at 140 characters, at the main layer, checked against its own 200-draw shuffle null.
Main test, window 200 characters: the same ripple statistic and null procedure, on the 12 test documents wrapped at 200 characters.
Main test, window 280 characters: the same ripple statistic and null procedure, on the 12 test documents wrapped at 280 characters.

Control, chance baseline: for each of the three windows, 200 draws that shuffle each document's own labels within that document, then the same maximum-power statistic per draw. This is the null every main test above is judged against; every draw's full power spectrum is saved.

Control, token position instead of characters: at the main layer, the same three windows and the same 200-draw shuffle-null procedure, but a token's label counts sub-word tokens since the last line break, not characters. Wavelengths are converted to characters using the measured characters-per-token rate at each window.

Represented-range check (the pre-registered escape hatch), at the main layer, window-280 test documents only: held-out fit quality inside each of eight 35-label bins, each checked against 50 draws of that same bin's own label-shuffle null. The bin spanning label 150 is recorded but excluded from the represented-or-not decision.

Reporting requirement, all arms: every ripple record, every control record, and the range-check record carries the anchor gate's pass-or-fail decision and its measured band written into that record's own values, not only into a separate summary file.
design.data: stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd), loaded exactly, never regenerated, re-wrapped, or paraphrased; halt if absent. Contents: 48 public-domain English prose documents, about 3,600 characters each, each materialized at nine wrap widths (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 200, 280 characters). Documents 0-35 (36 documents) are training; documents 36-47 (12 documents) are test; the split is a fixed block in book order. The text is disjoint by construction from seed D1's stimulus file, so every number here is a fresh-text check, not a re-read of D1's numbers.
does_not_test: Does not test any checkpoint besides step143000, or whether a ripple is a stable feature versus training-time debris; the checkpoint sweep is out of scope by the question's own statement.
Does not test any model besides this one 410-million-parameter substrate cell; other models or sizes are out of scope by the question's own statement.
Does not test any causal intervention on the model; only passive reading of activations is in scope by the question's own statement.
Does not re-run the prior fitted-probe cross-check from seed D1; the question drops it because its agreement was empty, its fit never converged, and no null was ever computable for it.
Does not decide INVARIANT versus PROPORTIONAL when exactly one window clears its null; that case is recorded UNDETERMINED by design, not resolved by collecting more data.
The exact ridge-strength grid points past 1000 are a GUESS; a coarser grid could miss the true best strength and understate every held-out fit quality, main layer and anchor layer alike.
Five-fold cross-validation for choosing ridge strength is a GUESS; the question fixes only a grid past 1000, not a fold count, and a different fold count could shift the winning strength slightly.

The base random seed (0) for every shuffle draw is a GUESS; a different seed could move a borderline window across its own clearing threshold, which is why the result is read from the invariance fork across windows, not from one window's raw pass or fail.
The 6-document holdout size for each of the 5 anchor resplits is a GUESS; a larger holdout would widen the measured dispersion and could turn a narrow miss into a pass, or the reverse.

The 10-character invariance cutoff and the 0.1 ratio cutoff are guesses carried unchanged from the question's own text; a true wavelength drifting by, say, 12 characters would be called non-invariant even if it were the same pattern plus noise.

The 3-character token-versus-character margin is a guess carried unchanged from the question's own text; a real character effect could be misattributed to token position near that margin, or the reverse.

The 200-draw shuffle null, per window per labeling, is a guess carried unchanged from the question's own text; it sets the finest detectable false-positive rate near 0.5 percent per window, so a real but rarer ripple could be missed.

The rule that derives each window's ripple profile length from training documents' own label range is this design's own addition, since the question requires a committed calibration step but does not spell out the derivation; a different derivation could search a different top period and change which periods the statistic can find.

The $4 budget is a GUESS built from this project's own prior costs for similar three-window runs on this checkpoint (about $0.55 to $0.6 actual), plus one hour of rented A100 time at $1.99 and headroom for one retry; a slower checkpoint download or a stuck resplit loop could still push real cost higher.

The hardware assumption (one A100 40 GB SXM4 box, $1.99 per hour, us-west-2, whole run finishing inside one hour) is a GUESS about capacity and speed; if the box lacks capacity or the run overruns the hour, the launcher's own cap governs, not this estimate.

endpoints.metric: Anchor gate: held-out fit quality (a held-out R-squared) at the anchor layer, width 140 only, on the 12 fresh test documents.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: The width-140 fit falls outside its own measured band. Every ripple, control, and range-check result this run produces is voided as an instrument fault, and no next seed on this question may build on it; this is not evidence about the model.
endpoints.threshold: Falls inside a band centred on 0.781, half-width 3 times the median absolute deviation of this same statistic across 5 resplits of the 36 training documents. A measured spread of exactly zero halts the run as WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE instead of using a zero-width band.

endpoints.metric: Maximum ripple power, over every whole-cycle period from 4 characters up to that window's committed profile length, at each of the three windows (140, 200, 280), against that window's own 200-draw shuffle null.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: The observed maximum ranks worse than 10th of 200 at a given window; no separable ripple at that window.
endpoints.threshold: The observed maximum ranks 10th or better among the 200 null draws (beats all but the top 5 percent).

endpoints.metric: Count, among the three windows, of how many clear their own shuffle null.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: 0 of 3 windows clear, AND the represented-range check shows label counts above 150 ARE represented. Together these give a decisive negative: no character-count ripple detectable up to 280 characters at this checkpoint.

endpoints.metric: Among windows that cleared their own null, the largest gap in characters between any two of their ripple wavelengths.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: The gap exceeds 10 characters for at least one pair of clearing windows; rules out one fixed wavelength shared across windows.
endpoints.threshold: At most 10 characters (a guessed cutoff carried from the question) counts as INVARIANT.

endpoints.metric: Among windows that cleared their own null, the largest gap between any two windows' wavelength-to-window-width ratios.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Ratios differ by more than 0.1 for at least one pair while wavelengths also differ by more than 10 characters; recorded as MIXED. Exactly one window clearing its null is recorded as UNDETERMINED, never as MIXED.
endpoints.threshold: Within 0.1 of each other (a guessed cutoff carried from the question) counts as PROPORTIONAL, once INVARIANT has already been ruled out.

endpoints.metric: Represented-range check: inside each of eight 35-label bins at window 280, held-out fit quality against that same bin's own 50-draw label-shuffle null, at the main layer.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: Every bin fully at or below label 140 is represented AND every bin fully above label 150 is not. Then a null ripple at window 200 or 280 is recorded as RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED, not as evidence against a ripple. If instead a bin above label 150 IS represented, that same null ripple stands as a genuine negative.
endpoints.threshold: A bin counts as represented when its fit quality exceeds the 95th percentile of its own 50 null draws; the bin spanning label 150 is recorded but excluded from the decision.

endpoints.metric: Per window, the gap in characters between the character-count ripple's wavelength and the token-position control's wavelength, after converting the token result to characters at the measured characters-per-token rate.
endpoints.refuting_outcome: The gap is 3 characters or less AND both labelings clear their null. The ripple at that window is credited to token position, not to counting characters.
endpoints.threshold: A gap of more than 3 characters (a guessed margin carried from the question), or the two labelings disagreeing on whether they clear their null, credits the ripple to counting characters.

design.hypothesis: At the Pythia-410m-deduped, step143000 checkpoint, this experiment asks: does a residual-stream ripple in the character-count code, wherever one clears its own shuffle null, keep one wavelength in characters across probe windows of 140, 200, and 280 characters (INVARIANT, a property of the model), or does its wavelength scale with the window (PROPORTIONAL, an artifact of the probe)? Two other outcomes are possible by the same rule: MIXED (neither pattern holds) and UNDETERMINED (exactly one window clears). If no window clears its null, that is a decisive negative up to 280 characters, unless the represented-range check shows label counts above 150 were never measurable, in which case the negative is recorded as RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED instead.
design.layers_strengths: Main layer: best held-out fit, swept over layers 0-24, ridge strength chosen from a grid extending past 1000 (exact points GUESS), fit pooled over all nine wrap widths on the 36 training documents, scored on the 12 test documents. Anchor layer: the same sweep and the same grid, but fit and scored using only the width-140 documents; used only for the anchor gate, never for any ripple test. Both selections pick the layer and strength with the best held-out fit on their own training data; whether the chosen strength sits at an interior grid point or at an edge is recorded for each selection.
models: EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped, HuggingFace revision step143000, base model, no fine-tuning or interventions -- one substrate cell only, per the question's own stated scope. The downloaded model config is authoritative; 24 transformer layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1). A mismatch between that memory and the downloaded config halts the run before any measurement.
design.sampling: No text is generated. Every measurement reads hidden activations from one deterministic forward pass per document per wrap width, so there are no temperature or top-p settings. Layers swept: 0 through 24, where 0 is the embedding output and 24 is the last transformer layer (both MEMORY, Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1); a mismatch against the downloaded model's own config halts the run first. Ridge strength is chosen by five-fold cross-validation on the 36 training documents (the five-fold choice is a GUESS; the question only requires a grid past 1000), from the grid {1, 10, 100, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000} (GUESS, exact points not fixed by the question). Two separate layer selections run: one pooled over all nine wrap widths (the main layer, used for every ripple test and the range check), one using only the width-140 documents (the anchor layer, used only for the anchor gate). Label-shuffle null for the three main ripple tests: 200 draws per window per labeling (character-count and token-position; the 200 figure is the question's own GUESS), each draw shuffling one document's labels within that document only, fixed base random seed 0 (GUESS, arbitrary, for reproducibility only). Label-shuffle null for the represented-range check: 50 draws per bin, 8 bins, window 280 only, 400 draws total, same seeding convention (50 draws and 8 bins are fixed by the question, not guessed). Anchor dispersion: 5 resplits of the 36 training documents (fixed by the question), each holding out 6 documents (GUESS split size) as a fresh internal test set, re-running the width-140 layer selection and fit on each split; the spread across these 5 values sets the anchor band's half-width. Each window's ripple profile length (how many periods the discrete Fourier transform searches) is committed by a calibration rule, not guessed: on training documents only, take the largest label value that occurs at that window's wrap width (or width plus one, for line-final newline tokens), and commit that count before any test-document ripple number is read. n per cell: 12 test documents per window for every main ripple test and its null; 36 training documents pooled over nine widths for the main layer selection; 36 training documents at width 140 only for the anchor layer selection and its 5 resplits; 8 bins of 35 label values each, from the 12 test documents at window 280, for the represented-range check.

departures.question: Should the number of periods searched at each window depend on the longest line length in training text, or be fixed some other way?
departures.what: The design invents its own rule for how many periods the frequency search covers at each probe window. It bases this on the longest line length seen in training text at that wrap width. The question never specifies this derivation. Tying the search range to the window's own size risks repeating the earlier run's unresolved problem (seed D1). That earlier problem was a maximum reading with no way to test it against chance.

departures.question: Should every chance-comparison shuffle start from the same fixed random point, or should several different starting points be checked?
departures.what: Every random shuffle used to build the chance comparison starts from the same fixed starting point, chosen arbitrarily. The question does not set this starting point. A different starting point could push a borderline probe window across the pass or fail line. That could push the final call from one outcome to another, such as from a shared wavelength to a mixed result.

departures.question: Is this list of test strengths (1, 10, 100, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000) fine enough to trust a pass or fail?
departures.what: The design picks a specific list of ridge-regression strength values to test: 1, 10, 100, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000. The question only says the list must reach past 1000. A different, finer list could find a better setting. That could change whether the held-out fit quality check passes or fails, which decides whether the whole run counts.

departures.question: Is holding out 6 of the 36 training documents, five separate times, the right amount to set the pass-fail range?
departures.what: To measure how wide the pass-fail range should be, the design reruns the check five times. Each time it holds out 6 of the 36 training documents as a stand-in test set. The question does not say how many documents to hold out. A different number could make the pass-fail range narrower or wider, changing whether the run's main result is allowed to stand.

departures.question: Is a $4 budget on one rented graphics computer, for about one hour, enough to safely finish all three probe windows?
departures.what: The plan sets a total spending cap of $4 and assumes one rented graphics computer at $1.99 an hour finishes everything within an hour. The question says nothing about cost or hardware. If a checkpoint download stalls or a step needs rerunning, the run could be cut off before all three probe windows finish.

gate: BUDGET_AND_DESIGN_APPROVAL: human commits a gate file answering, of record, every diff question, every non-reproducing grounding note, and every queued item (instrument validations included; "accepted as-is" is an answer) before mode=build.
seed:
Two prior results frame this question. First, the original study (Gurnee et al., "When Models Manipulate Manifolds", Transformer Circuits, Oct 2025; Claude 3.5 Haiku) found a curve in the residual stream tracking characters since the last newline, showing faint off-diagonal bands ("ringing") in its cosine-similarity structure, explained as Gibbs-style truncation: a similarity structure realizable in 150 dimensions forced into about 6. Second, a completed run in this project (seed D1, 2026-08-21; its committed numbers are restated here, and this file is their carrier) measured, on the final checkpoint of Pythia-410m-deduped: held-out probe R-squared 0.781 at layer 6 of 24 (embedding output is index 0); ambient dimension 1 at 95 percent variance (first component 95.3 percent); no ripple separable from a label-shuffle null at the single testable period (rank 109 of 200 at period 60); and a full-spectrum re-read showing the largest spectral power at period 120 - the profile's own length - which could not be ranked against any null because only in-band maxima were saved.

Seed D1's negative was censored by its own aperture: with ambient dimension 1, the theory's predicted ripple spacing equals the probe window divided by one - the window itself - at any window. Widening the window moves the prediction with it. So the decidable question is not "is there a ripple in a wider window" but invariance:

Question: at this same checkpoint, when the similarity structure of the character-count representation is measured at three apertures - probe windows of 140, 200, and 280 characters - and a periodicity clears its shuffle null at any aperture, is its wavelength INVARIANT in characters across apertures (an absolute property of the model's code), or PROPORTIONAL to the aperture (an artifact of the probe window)? And if no aperture clears its null, that is a decisive negative across every scale up to 280 characters - with one pre-registered escape, the represented-range check below, which decides whether the wide apertures were measuring anything at all.

Substrate, one cell only: EleutherAI/pythia-410m-deduped, HuggingFace revision step143000, base model, no interventions. The checkpoint sweep, the equilibrium-versus-fossil question, other models and sizes, and causal tests are out of scope. The downloaded config is authoritative; 24 layers and hidden size 1024 are MEMORY (Pythia paper, arXiv 2304.01373, table 1); mismatch is a halt. Layer indices count the embedding output as index 0; the best layer's location is recorded, never gated.

Stimuli, committed verbatim in stimulus_linewrap_v2.json (sha256 b0aa4255b5038d6fbc2e7314decf1011a5b5a13990098142e16ab44c6bba41dd): 48 public-domain ASCII prose documents of about 3,600 characters, each materialized at nine wrap widths (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 200, 280); documents 0-35 train, 36-47 test, a block split in book order; the text is disjoint by construction from seed D1's stimulus file (the generator replays D1's packing and starts after it), so the anchor leg below is a fresh-text replication. Load exactly; do not paraphrase, regenerate, re-wrap, or reconstruct; if absent, halt.

Definitions, fixed here:

1. Labels as in seed D1: a token's label is the count of characters on its line up to and including its last character, restarting after each newline; standalone newline tokens land at width plus one (measured fact, seed D1: 18 such positions). The label window per aperture is fixed by the calibration stage.

2. Curve readout: ridge regression from the residual stream after each layer to the label, fit on train documents pooled over all nine widths, R-squared on test documents, per layer. Ridge strength from calibration; grid must extend beyond 1000 (seed D1's grid ended at 1000 with quality still rising, delta 0.0033 - measured, results_seedD calibration record).

3. Represented-range check, at the best layer: held-out R-squared computed separately within each bin of 35 consecutive label values at aperture 280 (eight bins), where the bin's own variance is the denominator. Pre-registered reading, by rule not by value: a bin counts as represented when its within-bin held-out fit exceeds the 95th percentile of its own within-bin label-shuffle null (50 draws); the bin straddling 150 is recorded but excluded from the decision. If every bin fully at or below 140 is represented and every bin fully above 150 is not, counts beyond 150 are "not represented", and a null ripple at apertures 200 and 280 is then recorded as RANGE_NOT_REPRESENTED, not as evidence against the ripple. Context: the Pile's hard-wrapped training pressure sits near 70-72 characters per line (Gutenberg 2.17 percent of the mix; source: counting_manifold_formation_proposal.md, verified table).

4. Ripple statistic, per aperture A in {140, 200, 280}, at the best layer, test documents of width A only: per-label mean vectors; subtract the grand mean; cosine similarity matrix; off-diagonal profile m(delta) for delta 1 to max_delta (the calibration stage fixes max_delta per aperture and writes it into its committed record before any test-document number exists); subtract the best-fitting degree-2 polynomial (fixed here - seed D1 verified that a moving average removes exactly the predicted periods); discrete Fourier transform; the statistic is the MAXIMUM power over ALL whole-cycle periods from 4 characters to the profile length. No search band exists in this design - the band censorship of seed D1 is removed. Ambient dimension is measured and recorded per aperture; unlike seed D1 it constrains nothing.

5. Null, per aperture: labels shuffled within each document, 200 draws (GUESS), the same maximum-power statistic per draw. Separable means the observed maximum exceeds all but the top 5 percent of draws (policy, unchanged from seed D1). Every draw's FULL per-period power vector is saved, and the per-label mean vectors at the best layer are saved into the fetched results - both absences made seed D1's geometry unauditable afterward.

6. Invariance rule, over the apertures that clear their null: wavelengths in characters. All pairwise differences at most 10 characters (GUESS): INVARIANT. All wavelength-to-aperture ratios within 0.1 of each other (GUESS): PROPORTIONAL. Neither: MIXED. Exactly one aperture clears: UNDETERMINED. The headline decision is this fork, not mere presence; three 5-percent tests carry about a 14 percent family-wise false-positive rate, which the fork absorbs because it conditions on which apertures cleared.

7. Token-position control, per aperture: the same maximum-power statistic and null with tokens-since-newline labels; periods converted to characters at the measured characters-per-token; the character-count ripple is credited only where wavelengths differ by more than 3 characters (GUESS) or the two labelings disagree on clearing.

8. Anchor gate, by rule not by value. The anchor statistic is held-out fit at width 140 alone, judged at the layer the calibration stage selects on train documents at width 140 alone - the selection procedure is part of the anchor's definition, fixed here. The band is centred on the prior committed value 0.781; its half-width is measured, not guessed: 3 times the median absolute deviation of the anchor statistic across 5 resplits of the train documents (variance source: resamples of documents; rerun dispersion is zero for a deterministic probe, and a measured dispersion of exactly zero means the wrong source was chosen - halt WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE rather than emit a zero-width band). The band is computed and committed by the calibration record before any test-document row is read. A fresh-text anchor outside the measured band voids every ripple result as an instrument fault and blocks any next seed; it is not evidence about the model. The dispersion record ships with the results either way.

Dropped from seed D1, deliberately: the fitted-probe cross-check (its agreement was vacuous with one searchable period, its fit never converged, and no null was computable for it - all three measured in seed D1's post records).

Changed from the prior asking of this question, deliberately: the anchor band was a guessed plus-or-minus 0.08 and is now a measured-dispersion rule with its selection procedure pinned; the represented-range thresholds were guessed absolute values (0.5, 0.3) and are now per-bin shuffle nulls with the straddling bin excluded; each aperture's profile length must be committed by the calibration record before the run, not decided in setup notes. Everything else is unchanged on purpose, so the two askings differ only where the prior run's own failure pointed.

author_queue: Report the 5 anchor-resplit R^2 values, their MAD, the resulting band [center-3*MAD, center+3*MAD], and the observed width-140 test-set R^2 for step143000 -- confirm the band width is not so narrow (e.g. <0.02 half-width) that ordinary train/test sampling variance alone would fail it independent of model signal.

findings.confound: decidability by construction: is any endpoint outcome forced, unable to occur, or deciding a different question than the seed asks
findings.crux: The anchor gate's pass/fail band is set to 3x the MAD of the anchor statistic across only 5 resplits of the 36 training documents. With n=5, MAD is a very unstable, low-resolution dispersion estimate: it can easily come out tiny (if resplit fits cluster) or, per the design's own admission, exactly zero (triggering WRONG_VARIANCE_SOURCE). A tiny-but-nonzero MAD would produce a band so narrow that the width-140 held-out fit on the 12 disjoint test documents (which differ from the 6-doc training subsplits in identity and size) is likely to land outside it from ordinary sampling variation alone -- voiding every ripple/control/range-check result as an 'instrument fault' regardless of whether the model actually carries an invariant or proportional character-count ripple. That would make the anchor gate decide 'is n=5 resplit dispersion representative of held-out generalization noise', not 'does the model actually clear its own null', and could force VOID on a run that would otherwise cleanly reach INVARIANT/PROPORTIONAL/MIXED/UNDETERMINED. Whether this actually happens depends on the realized MAD and test-set R^2, which are not in the committed evidence (only the pre-registered band recipe, no resplit outputs).

findings.confound: coordinates and scale: could the chosen layers/strengths/windows make every cell degenerate or null regardless of hypothesis
findings.crux: The evidence block is the pre-registration/design only — it contains hypothesis, arms, endpoints, and sampling/guess disclosures, but no actual measured statistic (no anchor-gate R², no ripple power, no chosen layer index, no ridge-strength grid point) has been reported. Whether the coordinate/scale confound explains a null/degenerate result depends entirely on where the main/anchor layer selection lands (interior layer vs. edge like layer 0 or 24) and whether the winning ridge strength sits at an interior grid point or at the grid's edge (per "whether the chosen strength sits at an interior grid point or at an edge is recorded for each selection") — none of which is given here, so I cannot tell whether this run's own coordinates make the cells degenerate.
